column1: # R0 corpus BASE VERDICTS at 33560b12 (epic #1678, ADR-0051), measured by TestR0Corpus{Own,Uniq,Dup}.
# Re-pinned at R0 fix round 5 (the independent review's items 2/4 and 3(d)), each with its reason:
#   own/outer_nonstrict_rows on dag, dag-shuffled, dag-morsel4: digest only, wrong:414af4440568 -> wrong:564413ecb116.
#     The arms answer zero rows; the capture now keeps a zero-row result's RowDescription (r0Query), so the
#     digest of the wrong answer includes its declaration (cols=["id"] types=["int8"]). Verdict and class unchanged.
#   uniq and dup h2_base2_control on spilled512k: unpinned-flap -> flap:refused:42000 (bounded). Measured at
#     dc980141+R0 over 20 fresh runs per fixture: 19 x refused 42000 "memory budget exceeded" (hash join build),
#     1 x PostgreSQL's answer, on each fixture.
# Re-pinned at #1681 line 1681a (a semi/anti residual with a NULL operand is UNKNOWN, not its zero value):
#   own/semi, semi_rows, semi_base, anti, anti_rows on all six arms: wrong:<digest> executor -> right (30 cells).
# A pin of "wrong" or "refused" is a RECORDED KNOWN DEFECT on issue #1678 (or the issue its class names),
# NOT an acceptance. The test fails when a cell's verdict differs from its pin in EITHER direction: the
# stage that repairs a cell re-pins it with the reason; nothing updates itself.
# Re-pinning is a deliberate two-step act: (1) run TestR0Corpus{Own,Uniq,Dup} with R0_PINS_WRITE=1; each
# writes its fixture's measured verdicts to r0_corpus_pins_<fixture>.tsv in a fresh directory it creates under
# os.TempDir() and logs the full path; (2) review those artifacts and copy the rows here by hand. No R0 writer
# (R0_PINS_WRITE, R0_PG_WRITE, R0_FIXTURE_WRITE, R0_COST_WRITE, the report switches) takes a path: any value
# but 1 fails the test before it measures (TestR0WritersRefuseCommittedTargets).
# CPU capacity: the arm NAMED dag-morsel4 is measured under whatever capacity the test process has. A worker's
# token pool is GOMAXPROCS-2, and a fragment runs serial at width 1+capacity <= 1, so with GOMAXPROCS <= 2 that
# arm executes serial (it is then the dag arm with MorselWorkers=4 configured but not engaged). These pins were
# measured at 33560b12 and confirmed unchanged at R0 fix round 7 at GOMAXPROCS=24 (the host default, 24 CPUs:
# morsel-parallel) and at GOMAXPROCS=2 (serial): no dag-morsel4 pin differs between the two.
# TestR0ConfiguredArmsActuallyEngage raises GOMAXPROCS to 6 for its own run, so the engagement itself is verified
# verdict: right | wrong:<digest of the arm's canonical answer> | refused:<SQLSTATE> (PostgreSQL answered,
#   or raised another SQLSTATE) | routed-right | routed-wrong:<digest> (a DAG arm that routed to the bound
#   plan L: L's answer, not evidence about the DAG) | flap:refused:<SQLSTATE> (a cell measured to alternate
#   between PostgreSQL's answer and ONE named resource refusal; its class column is "-|<refusal class>"; it
#   accepts exactly PostgreSQL's answer or that refusal with the memory-budget message class (r0FlapAccepts),
#   and any other outcome, a wrong successful answer included, fails).
# class (mechanical, r0Class): capability (every arm refuses alike with a SQLSTATE PostgreSQL does not raise);
#   error-domain (r2's 18 and the judge's error pairs where PostgreSQL or the arm raises 22012: D4, the
#   maintainer's ruling 2026-11-21, disposition undecided, PostgreSQL's result kept in r0_corpus_pg17.tsv);
#   executor (the semi/anti residual statements, #1681's line; or spilled512k wrong where single is right);
#   emission (a DAG arm differs from PostgreSQL where localD is PostgreSQL's answer); logical (localD, or the
#   single-process arm, differs from PostgreSQL; a routed DAG cell follows L).
# note (localD rows): the seam's status (established | late-subplan | vetoed | refused-before-planning) and
#   dag-routes when the stage DAG would route the statement to L.
